paper_metadata.title: Improvement in ductility of high strength polycrystalline Ni-rich Ni3Al alloy produced by EB-PVD

evidence.quote: A 300 lm Ni-rich Ni 3Al sheet was produced by electron beam physical vapor deposition (EB-PVD) and followed by different heat treatments

The evaporation process was carried out in EB-PVD working chamber under vacuum ranging 2 10-3 Pa to 2 10-2 Pa. The substrates were adjusted at 600 C during deposition.
After deposition, the sheets were detached from the substrates and heat-treated at 900 C, 1000 C and 1100 C for 4 h with a vacuum pressure of 3 10-3 Pa.

The XRD images ( Fig. 4 ) of as-deposited and heat treated Ni 3Al sheets show that all samples consist of c and c0 phases.
A very small amount of tough c phase exists in the as-deposited sample (Fig. 5 a).
Results indicated that the as-deposited Ni 3Al alloy exhibited non-equilibrium directional columnar crystal

The volume fraction of c phase in HT900, HT1000 and HT1100 increases from16.7%, 26.4% to 28.1% with increasing heat treatment temperatures, and tough c phase with irregular shape distributes in c0/c0 grain boundaries

As shown in Fig. 5d, the distribution of c phase in HT1100, like a mesh network, increases the c0-c interface area and effectively suppresses crack propagation during tensile
transited to equiaxed crystal with uniformly distributed tough c phase after heat treatment
Benefit from continuous mesh network microstructure, the heat treated sample obtained large elongation, the highest of which reached 14.6%.
The sizes of secondary c0 phase particles in HT1000 and HT1100 are 20 nm and 50 nm, respectively
The sizes of secondary c0 phase particles in HT1000 and HT1100 are 20 nm and 50 nm, respectively
When a crack nucleates at a c0-c0 grain boundary and propagates rapidly along the c0-c0 boundaries, the crack may be blunted at the c0-c interface due to the network of c phase.
The as-deposited Ni 3Al sheet exhibits elastic deformation ( 0.5%) and flat fracture ( Fig. 2a).
the tensile elongation increases significantly with increasing heat treatment temperature, up to 14.6% in HT1100
the elongation of HT1100 (14.6%) takes more than four times as much as that of HT1000 (3.0%)
The tensile strength of the as-deposited sample is higher than 900 MPa in Fig. 1.
The yield strength values of HT900, HT1000, and HT1100 are 844 MPa, 682 MPa and 512 MPa, respectively.

The yield strength values of HT900, HT1000, and HT1100 are 844 MPa, 682 MPa and 512 MPa, respectively.
The flow stress of HT1000 shows little change after yielding, while that of HT1100 increases from 512 MPa to 828 MPa.

Therefore, the increasing volume fraction of c phase effectively enhances the ductility and the elongation of Ni 3Al alloy sheet.
When a crack nucleates at a c0-c0 grain boundary and propagates rapidly along the c0-c0 boundaries, the crack may be blunted at the c0-c interface due to the network of c phase.

According to Hall–Petch relationship, the yield strength decreases with increasing grain size. Therefore, compared with previous literatures ( Table 1 ), the EB-PVD sheets exhibit high yield strength due to fine-grain strengthening.
The difference in flow stress between HT1000 and HT1100 samples could be associated with secondary c0 precipitation strengthening, which is similar like nickel based superalloys

there are increasing number of additional tearing ridges in grain boundaries ( Fig. 6 d, f and h), which enhances the effective slip length for dislocation motion and promotes the ductility of the heat treated samples
